jobs.title: Program Manager, Provider Partnerships
jobs.description:
ABOUT OPENROUTER

OpenRouter is the unified interface for LLMs. We route billions of tokens every month, helping developers and enterprises access, manage, and optimize their AI use across 400+ models and providers — without worrying about lock-in, capacity constraints, downtime, or complex integrations.

Our provider ecosystem is the foundation of that marketplace. As the number of model labs and inference providers we work with grows, the relationships behind them have to scale like a product — with consistent tiers, lifecycles, and standards — not as a set of one-off deals.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re hiring a Program Manager to turn our Provider Program into a product. Today, provider relationships are managed one at a time; your job is to give them a repeatable structure so the ecosystem scales without adding headcount for every new partner.

You’ll own the standard provider lifecycle end to end — sourcing, onboarding, activation, QBR, and renewal — along with provider tiering (our “buckets”), SLAs, and the compliance cadence that keeps the program trustworthy. You’ll be the one person with context across every partnership, able to run program-wide operations (re-paper all providers, roll out a new compliance attestation, launch a new tier) without pulling individual partnership owners off their accounts.

You’ll also run our flagship programs, starting with MPEAP (Model Provider Early Access Program) and our verified/certified provider tracks. This is a high-ownership role that sits at the intersection of Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, and Security.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own the provider lifecycle. Define and operate the standard path from sourcing → onboarding → activation → QBR → renewal, with clear stage gates, owners, and SLAs.

 - Design provider tiering. Build and maintain the tiering framework (the “buckets”) that determines how providers are classified, what they get, and what’s expected of them.

 - Build programmatic structure that scales. Turn one-off relationships into repeatable systems — templates, playbooks, self-serve onboarding, and automated provider comms — so the program grows without linear headcount.

 - Run cross-program operations. Execute program-wide changes (re-paper all providers, launch a new tier, roll out a new compliance attestation) as a single coordinated motion.

 - Run the flagship programs. Operate MPEAP and the verified/certified provider tracks, from intake criteria to ongoing management.

 - Own the compliance cadence. Keep SLAs, attestations, and provider obligations on schedule and auditable.

 - Set the operating cadence. Run the rhythm of the team — reviews, reporting, and the operating cadence that keeps everyone aligned.

 - Partner cross-functionally. Work across Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, and Security to unblock providers and ship program improvements.




ABOUT YOU

 - Programs + strategy background. You’ve built and run programs or strategy at a large, complex organization (e.g. a Salesforce-scale org) and know how to impose structure on ambiguity.

 - Highly organized systems thinker. You instinctively turn recurring work into repeatable, automatable processes and see where linear effort should become leverage.

 - Cross-functional operator. You’re comfortable owning operations that span Product, Engineering, Legal, Finance, and Security, and driving them to closure without formal authority.

 - High agency and bias to ship. You take end-to-end ownership, move fast, and thrive in a small, fast-moving team with intentionally fluid boundaries.

 - Strong written communication. You can turn complex, multi-stakeholder programs into clear docs, playbooks, and comms.

 - Bonus: familiarity with the AI ecosystem — model labs, inference providers, and what it takes to onboard and certify them.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - A front-row seat to the AI ecosystem and direct relationships with the model labs and providers shaping it.

 - High ownership and the room to define a program from the ground up.

 - Remote-first (US), competitive salary and equity, fully covered health/dental/vision, unlimited PTO, a WFH budget, and quarterly offsites.



If you don’t think you meet all of the criteria above but are still interested in the role, please apply. Nobody checks every box, and we’re looking for someone excited to build this program with us.

jobs.title: Customer Success Manager
jobs.description:
THIS ROLE MUST BE BASED IN THE SAN FRANCISCO BAY AREA (CALIFORNIA)




ABOUT OPENROUTER

OpenRouter is the open AI routing and infrastructure layer that enterprises use to access, manage, and optimize the best large language models across providers—without lock-in, capacity constraints, or unnecessary cost. We power some of the most advanced AI teams in the world by giving them the flexibility to move fast, scale confidently, and stay future-proof as models evolve.

As enterprise adoption of AI accelerates, OpenRouter sits at the center of how organizations operationalize LLMs across research, product, and production workloads.




ABOUT THE ROLE 

As a Customer Success Manager at OpenRouter, you will own a portfolio of hyper-growth, Enterprise accounts. Your goal is simple but demanding: Drive adoption, unlock outcomes and value, and lead inference growth. You will be the bridge between complex technical systems, clear business outcomes and commercial growth.




WHAT YOU'LL DO 

 - Strategy and Adoption: You need to get into the weeds of what customers are building. Whether it’s an AI agent or a coding tool, you’ll create the plan that helps them use OpenRouter to its full potential.

 - Revenue and Outcome Ownership: You are responsible for keeping our customers around and helping them grow. You’ll lead the commercial talks and find ways to expand their usage across different product lines.

 - Strategic & Tactical Execution: One hour you’ll be presenting an ROI analysis to a CTO; the next, you’ll be diving into API documentation to help a lead engineer optimize their model routing. You enjoy translating from strategic to technical and back (on repeat).

 - Value Realization: Define and track "Success Criteria" for every customer. You will turn abstract AI goals into concrete ROI metrics, ensuring OpenRouter is a mission-critical partner and an important part of their AI strategy.

 - The Feedback Loop: Act as the data focused voice of the customer for our GTM, Product and Engineering teams, distilling learnings and friction points into roadmap priorities.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

We are looking for a proactive AI Customer Success Manager. You don't wait for a customer to ask for help; you identify a drop in token usage or a new model release and reach out with a plan and strategy to drive adoption, value and growth.




REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - AI-Native DNA: You have previously worked at an AI-first company (LLM labs, AI infrastructure, or high-growth GenAI apps). You understand the nuances of tokens, latency, context windows, and model routing.

 - Technical Platform Expertise: You come from a background in technical SaaS or API-first platforms. You are comfortable talking to developers and product managers in their own language.

 - Revenue Focused: You have a proven track record of owning a quota. You are comfortable navigating procurement, legal, and executive stakeholders to get a deal done.

 - Playbook Builder: You don’t just fix things once. You build the systems and guides that help us scale this to the next thousand customers.




CORE COMPETENCIES

 - Strategic Agility: The ability to zoom out to the 10,000-foot view of the AI market and zoom in to the tactical details of a customer's implementation.

 - Commercial Grit: A proactive mindset regarding renewals and expansions. You see a renewal as an opportunity to re-sell the value, not a clerical task.

 - Analytical Rigor: You use data to tell a story. You can analyze usage trends to predict churn or identify a perfect moment for an upsell.



If you don't think you meet all of the criteria below but still are interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box, and we're looking for someone who is excited to join the team.

jobs.title: Director, Growth Marketing
jobs.description:
ABOUT OPENROUTER

OpenRouter is the open AI routing and infrastructure layer that enterprises use to access, manage, and optimize the best large language models across providers—without lock-in, capacity constraints, or unnecessary cost. We power some of the most advanced AI teams in the world by giving them the flexibility to move fast, scale confidently, and stay future-proof as models evolve.

As enterprise adoption of AI accelerates, OpenRouter sits at the center of how organizations operationalize LLMs across research, product, and production workloads.




ABOUT THE ROLE

OpenRouter grows because developers find it, try it, and route more of their work through it. More than 10 million users and 250k+ apps process 200T+ tokens on the platform every month, nearly all of it starting in self-serve. You’ll own turning that reach into revenue: more of the right developers discovering OpenRouter, signing up, buying their first credits, and growing their usage.

You’ll run the self-serve growth engine: paid media and sponsorships, AEO/SEO, conversion optimization on key pages and flows, and the measurement and forecasting that keeps it all optimized. That’s roughly 75% of the role. The other 25% is partnering with our enterprise team as an execution and thought partner on demand gen.

This is a Director-level, player/coach role with a paid budget of $5M+ for 2027. In year one you’re hands-on: buying media, shipping tests, building the measurement stack, managing agencies. As the engine proves out, you build the team around it.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own self-serve revenue growth: build and run the marketing engine that reaches developers at scale, moves them from first touch to signup, first credit purchase, and expanding usage.

 - Plan and buy paid media across channels developers respect: search, social, newsletter and podcast/creator sponsorships, audio, OOH, and event sponsorships, spanning awareness and direct response. You own the budget and the agency/vendor bench.

 - Own the AEO/SEO roadmap for openrouter.ai http://openrouter.ai: classic organic search plus answer-engine visibility,executing with content, engineering, and outside specialists.

 - Run conversion optimization on key pages and flows (homepage, model pages, pricing, signup, credit purchase) in partnership with product and engineering, on a standing experimentation cadence.

 - Own measurement for all paid activity: attribution design, incrementality and holdout testing, channel reporting, and the quarterly forecasting and planning cycle for the paid budget.

 - Support enterprise demand gen as an execution and thought partner: MQL/MQA generation programs and the measurement connecting marketing touches to pipeline.




WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - 8+ years in growth or performance marketing, including meaningful time at a developer tools, API-first, or technical B2B SaaS company.

 - You’ve been directly accountable for self-serve or usage-based revenue (signup, activation, and spend) as your primary metric.

 - You’ve owned an annual multi-channel paid budget of $5M+, or scaled a program from seven figures into that range, and can walk through your CAC, payback math, and the channels you killed.

 - Hands-on with the measurement stack: product analytics (PostHog, GA4, Hex, or similar), attribution design, and at least one incrementality or holdout test you designed yourself.

 - You’ve owned or directed SEO for a technical product, and you have a working point of view on AEO: what changes when the search result is a ChatGPT answer.

 - You’ve built and run CRO/experimentation programs with real statistical discipline: hypothesis, test design, readout, decision.

 - Player/coach: comfortable executing solo today and building the function (agencies, contractors, eventual hires) as it scales.




NICE TO HAVE 

 - You’ve marketed to AI engineers specifically, or you’ve built something against an LLM API yourself (bonus if it was through OpenRouter).

 - Brand campaign experience: OOH, audio, or major sponsorships, measured with brand-lift studies or geo holdouts.

 - Demand gen or ABM experience feeding an enterprise sales motion.

 - Time inside a consumption-pricing business (Twilio, Datadog, Vercel-style) where marketing was judged on usage rather than lead volume.



If you don't think you meet all of the criteria below but still are interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box, and we're looking for someone who is excited to join the team.

jobs.title: GRC Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT OPENROUTER

OpenRouter is the leading AI routing and infrastructure layer that enterprises use to access, manage, and optimize the best large language models across providers—without lock-in, capacity constraints, or unnecessary cost. We power the most advanced AI teams in the world by giving them the flexibility to move fast, scale confidently, and stay future-proof as models evolve.

As enterprise adoption of AI accelerates, OpenRouter sits at the center of how organizations operationalize LLMs across research, product, and production workloads.




ABOUT THE ROLE

You own our compliance program day to day. Drata and Safebase are yours. SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, CCPA, BIPA, and the EU AI Act are yours. You'll report to the Head of IT & Security, and you'll run the program with very little daily management.

The controls are the easy part. The real work is getting an engineer mid-sprint to pull evidence, getting the whole company through training before the deadline, and doing it in a way that makes people take your next request seriously instead of ignoring it. If your ideal job is overseeing a program that someone else operates, this is not the role for you. We are looking for a strategic builder ready to roll up their sleeves.

We also work in a space where the regulation is still being written. A meaningful share of what you'll face has no established playbook, and you'll be the person deciding what a novel requirement actually means for our business.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own Drata end to end — administration, integrations, monitoring test health, and the manual evidence collection automation doesn't reach.

 - Curate the SafeBase knowledge base so sales can self-serve most customer security questionnaires — and be the escalation point for the ones they can't.

 - Drive personnel compliance: policy acknowledgments, device compliance, and recurring security and compliance training. This means chasing people down and building the habit, not just running the report.

 - Lead recurring ceremonies: user access reviews, penetration tests, BCDR and incident response tabletops, annual policy review and updates, risk assessments.

 - Work directly with Engineering on product-related compliance questions, from data handling to customer commitments.

 - Maintain audit readiness across SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, CCPA, BIPA, and the EU AI Act.

 - Translate emerging AI regulation into controls we can actually operate, rather than waiting for someone else's checklist.

 - Partner with HR, Legal, Customer Support, and Finance so compliance fits into work that's already happening.
   
    


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

 - Several years in GRC or compliance, hands-on — you've built and run programs, not just governed them.

 - At least one SOC 2 audit cycle owned end to end, evidence through fieldwork.

 - Admin-level fluency in a compliance automation platform (Drata strongly preferred).

 - Technical enough to hold a real conversation with engineers about architecture and data flows.

 - Proven cross-functional influence without becoming the person everyone avoids.

 - Comfortable when requirements shift and precedent doesn't exist.
   
    


NICE TO HAVE

 - PCI DSS in a startup environment

 - HIPAA as a Business Associate

 - EU AI Act or other emerging AI regulation

 - CISA, CISSP, or CIPP

 - First compliance hire experience

 - Scripting for evidence collection
   
    

If you don't think you meet all of the criteria below but still are interested in the job, please apply. Nobody checks every box, and we're looking for someone who is excited to join the team.
